title: Error Handling (Part 1) - Option, Result, and propagation
learning_objectives: Represent a value that may be absent with `Option`.
Represent an operation that may fail with `Result`.
Handle outcomes with `match` and propagate compatible errors with `?`.
Distinguish recoverable errors from situations where a panic is appropriate.
explanation: Rust makes ordinary failure explicit in a function's return type. `Option<T>` represents either a value or its absence, while `Result<T, E>` represents success or an error that can carry information. Matching handles either outcome directly, and `?` returns an error to the caller when an operation fails.

examples.title: Handle an optional lookup
Use `?` to propagate an error

compiler_error_examples: error[E0277]: the `?` operator can only be used in a function that returns `Result` or `Option`
completion_criteria: Exercise tests cover valid input, missing input, and malformed input
Learner can explain why missing and invalid input are distinct outcomes
Exercise propagates parsing errors without panicking
